title: Shemirat Halashon 28

chapters.title: Intending Constructive Benefit (To'elet)
chapters.about: fifth rule of to'elet, helping victims, encouraging teshuva through social pressure

chapters.title: Victim's Knowledge and Rechilut
chapters.about: distinction when victim already knows versus when harm is still unknown

chapters.title: Telling Unsympathetic People
chapters.about: prohibition when listeners will not help or will cause further strife

chapters.title: Family Ties in Halakha
chapters.about: misconceptions about helping relatives, equal application of lashon hara laws

chapters.title: Preemptive Warning to Prevent Financial Loss
chapters.about: disclosing theft or ongoing harm to protect an unaware victim

chapters.title: Preempting a Known Gossiper
chapters.about: warning listeners in advance to prevent kabalat lashon hara

chapters.title: When Rebuke Is Ineffective
chapters.about: requirement to speak in front of three people when rebuke will not work

chapters.title: Exceptions for Fear of Retaliation
chapters.about: modifying requirements when dealing with a dangerous or powerful offender

summary: This class explores the conditions under which speaking about another person's improper behavior is permitted for a constructive purpose (to'elet) according to Sefer Shemirat Halashon. Rabbi Soffer addresses how social pressure can encourage teshuva, whether family ties change the rules of speech, and how to preemptively protect people from a habitual gossiper. The lesson also details what to do when direct rebuke will not work and how fear of retaliation affects these halakhot.
subjects: Speaking in front of three people
questions: When is it permitted to share negative information for a constructive purpose?
Do the rules of lashon hara change if a family member was harmed?
Can you warn people in advance about someone who habitually spreads gossip?
What should be done if rebuking the transgressor will clearly not work?
Why does speaking in front of three people change the halakhic status of a statement?
